questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was established in which year?
questions.explanation: SAARC was established on 8 December 1985 in Dhaka, Bangladesh. 1983 is wrong because that year saw only the preparatory foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi; 1987 is wrong as it was the year of the third SAARC summit; 1990 is wrong as SAARC was already five years old by then.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about SAARC:

(i) Its permanent secretariat is located in Kathmandu, Nepal.
(ii) India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan are its members.
(iii) SAARC was founded with 9 member nations.
(iv) The first SAARC summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The SAARC secretariat is in Kathmandu (i-correct), it has 8 members including Afghanistan which joined in 2007 (ii-correct), and the first summit was held in Dhaka in 1985 (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because SAARC was founded with 7 members (Afghanistan joined later in 2007, making it 8).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is located in:
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat is located in Jakarta, Indonesia. Bangkok (Thailand) is wrong — it hosts UNESCAP; Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia) is wrong — it is the capital but not ASEAN HQ; Manila (Philippines) is wrong — it hosts the Asian Development Bank.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): SAARC has not been able to achieve significant progress in regional cooperation compared to ASEAN.
Reason (R): Political tensions between India and Pakistan have often hindered the functioning of SAARC.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: SAARC has indeed lagged behind ASEAN in regional integration (A is correct), and the India-Pakistan rivalry is widely recognized as the primary obstacle to SAARC's progress (R is correct and directly explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R does explain A; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following countries are founding members of ASEAN?

(i) Indonesia
(ii) Thailand
(iii) Vietnam
(iv) Philippines

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967 by Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines, Malaysia, and Singapore (the Bangkok Declaration). Vietnam (iii) is wrong because it joined ASEAN much later in 1995. Options containing (iii) are therefore incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following international organizations with their headquarters:

Column I:
(a) SAARC
(b) ASEAN
(c) World Trade Organization (WTO)
(d) International Monetary Fund (IMF)

Column II:
(i) Washington D.C., USA
(ii) Kathmandu, Nepal
(iii) Geneva, Switzerland
(iv) Jakarta, Indonesia

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: SAARC is headquartered in Kathmandu (a-ii), ASEAN in Jakarta (b-iv), WTO in Geneva (c-iii), and IMF in Washington D.C. (d-i). Option 2 incorrectly swaps WTO and IMF headquarters; Option 3 incorrectly swaps SAARC and ASEAN; Option 4 incorrectly places ASEAN in Geneva.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration) was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Bangkok Declaration establishing ASEAN was signed on 8 August 1967. 1965 is wrong — that year saw Singapore's separation from Malaysia; 1969 is wrong — ASEAN was already two years old; 1971 is wrong — that year saw the ZOPFAN Declaration by ASEAN, not its founding.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about ASEAN:

(i) ASEAN currently has 10 member nations.
(ii) The ASEAN motto is 'One Vision, One Identity, One Community'.
(iii) India is a full member of ASEAN.
(iv) The ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) was established to promote regional trade.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ASEAN has 10 members (i-correct), its motto is 'One Vision, One Identity, One Community' (ii-correct), and AFTA was established in 1992 to promote trade (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because India is a Dialogue Partner of ASEAN, not a full member.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement under SAARC came into force in which year?
questions.explanation: SAFTA came into force on 1 January 2006. 2004 is wrong — that was the year SAFTA was signed at the 12th SAARC summit in Islamabad; 2008 is wrong — trade liberalization was already in progress; 2010 is wrong — it is unrelated to SAFTA's commencement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): ASEAN has been more successful than SAARC in promoting economic integration among its members.
Reason (R): ASEAN members have relatively fewer bilateral political disputes compared to SAARC members.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: ASEAN has achieved deeper economic integration (AFTA, single market initiatives) than SAARC (A is correct). The absence of a dominant bilateral rivalry like India-Pakistan within ASEAN has facilitated cooperation (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because the fewer disputes directly explain ASEAN's success; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first SAARC summit was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The first SAARC summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh on 7–8 December 1985. Kathmandu is wrong — it hosts the secretariat but not the first summit; New Delhi is wrong — India hosted the second summit in 1986; Colombo is wrong — Sri Lanka hosted the third summit.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The principle of decision-making in SAARC is based on __________ among all member states.
questions.explanation: SAARC operates on the principle of unanimity — all members must agree for decisions to be taken. Simple majority is wrong as it is not used in SAARC; two-thirds majority is wrong — that applies in some UN contexts; weighted voting is wrong — that system is used in IMF/World Bank.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the SAARC charter:

(i) Bilateral and contentious issues are excluded from SAARC deliberations.
(ii) Decisions at all levels are taken on the basis of unanimity.
(iii) SAARC cooperation requires ratification by all member states.
(iv) SAARC has a provision for collective military action against external threats.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The SAARC charter excludes bilateral and contentious issues (i-correct), requires unanimity (ii-correct), and cooperation requires ratification (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because SAARC has no military alliance provision — it is focused on economic and social cooperation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are objectives of ASEAN?

(i) To promote economic growth and regional peace
(ii) To provide mutual assistance in training and research
(iii) To establish a common military defense system
(iv) To collaborate for better utilization of agriculture and industries

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: ASEAN aims to promote economic growth and peace (i-correct), provide mutual training and research assistance (ii-correct), and collaborate on agriculture and industry (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because ASEAN does not have a collective military defense pact — it follows the principle of non-interference.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following SAARC member countries with their year of joining:

Column I:
(a) Afghanistan
(b) Bangladesh
(c) Maldives
(d) Bhutan

Column II:
(i) 1985 (founding member)
(ii) 1985 (founding member)
(iii) 1985 (founding member)
(iv) 2007

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 (a-iv), while Bangladesh, Maldives, and Bhutan are all founding members from 1985 (b-i, c-ii, d-iii). Option 2 wrongly places Afghanistan as a founding member; Option 3 incorrectly rearranges the founding members; Option 4 wrongly puts Maldives as 2007 entrant.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The current number of member states in ASEAN is:
questions.explanation: ASEAN has 10 member states: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. 8 is wrong — that was the number before Cambodia and Laos joined; 9 is wrong — there was briefly 9 members after Vietnam joined; 12 is wrong — no expansion has taken ASEAN to 12.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a founding member of SAARC but not of ASEAN.
Reason (R): India is geographically located in South Asia, not in Southeast Asia.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India co-founded SAARC in 1985 and is not an ASEAN member (A is correct). India's South Asian location explains why it is part of SAARC (South Asian grouping) and not ASEAN (Southeast Asian grouping) (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because the geographical reasoning directly explains the membership; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The SAARC University is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The South Asian University (SAARC University) is located in New Delhi, India. Kathmandu is wrong — it hosts the SAARC Secretariat, not the university; Dhaka is wrong — it hosted the first summit; Colombo is wrong — it has no SAARC university campus.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about BIMSTEC:

(i) It stands for Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation.
(ii) India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, and Thailand are its members.
(iii) It was established in 1997.
(iv) Its secretariat is located in New Delhi, India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC stands for Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (i-correct), includes India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan (ii-correct — the five named are indeed members), and was established in 1997 (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because BIMSTEC's secretariat is in Dhaka, Bangladesh, not New Delhi.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) primarily deals with:
options: Security and political dialogue in the Asia-Pacific
questions.correctAnswer: Security and political dialogue in the Asia-Pacific
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) was established in 1994 as a platform for security dialogue in the Asia-Pacific region. Agricultural trade is wrong — that falls under AFTA; educational exchange is wrong — that is handled by other ASEAN mechanisms; environmental protection is wrong — ARF's mandate is security-focused.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the International Labour Organization (ILO):

(i) It was established in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles.
(ii) Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.
(iii) India is a founding member of the ILO.
(iv) It is an agency of ASEAN.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ILO was established in 1919 (i-correct), is headquartered in Geneva (ii-correct), and India is a founding member (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because ILO is a specialized agency of the United Nations, not ASEAN.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The SAARC Disaster Management Centre (SDMC) is located in:
questions.explanation: The SAARC Disaster Management Centre (now renamed SAARC Centre for Disaster Management) is located in New Delhi, India. Kathmandu is wrong — it hosts the Secretariat; Dhaka is wrong — it hosts BIMSTEC secretariat; Islamabad is wrong — it has no SAARC centre.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following regional organizations with their number of member countries:

Column I:
(a) SAARC
(b) ASEAN
(c) G-20
(d) BRICS

Column II:
(i) 5
(ii) 8
(iii) 10
(iv) 20

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: SAARC has 8 members (a-ii), ASEAN has 10 members (b-iii), G-20 has 20 members (c-iv), and BRICS originally had 5 members (d-i). Option 2 wrongly assigns 10 to SAARC; Option 3 incorrectly swaps G-20 and BRICS numbers; Option 4 wrongly assigns 5 members to SAARC.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Look East Policy' of India, now renamed 'Act East Policy', is primarily aimed at strengthening relations with:
questions.explanation: India's 'Act East Policy' (formerly 'Look East Policy') focuses on strengthening ties with ASEAN and broader East Asian nations. European Union is wrong — India has a separate strategic partnership; SAARC nations is wrong — they are South Asian neighbors; African Union is wrong — India engages separately through India-Africa summits.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the GDP (in billion USD, approximate) of select SAARC nations in 2023:

India → 3,500
Bangladesh → 450
Pakistan → 340
Sri Lanka → 75
Nepal → 40

What is the approximate percentage share of India's GDP in the total GDP of these five countries?
questions.explanation: Total GDP = 3500 + 450 + 340 + 75 + 40 = 4405 billion USD. India's share = (3500/4405) × 100 ≈ 79.5% ≈ 79%. Option 72% is wrong (too low — uses wrong total); 75% is wrong (underestimates India's dominance); 83% is wrong (overestimates — excludes some countries' GDP).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which country holds the rotating chairmanship of ASEAN in alphabetical order of member states' names?
options: The chairmanship rotates alphabetically by country name
The chairmanship is held permanently by Indonesia
The chairmanship rotates by GDP size
The chairmanship is elected by voting
questions.correctAnswer: The chairmanship rotates alphabetically by country name
questions.explanation: ASEAN chairmanship rotates annually among member states in alphabetical order. Permanent Indonesian chairmanship is wrong — no country permanently chairs ASEAN; GDP-based rotation is wrong — it is alphabetical; election by voting is wrong — there is no such provision.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The SAARC charter was adopted in which city?
questions.explanation: The SAARC Charter was adopted at the first summit held in Dhaka, Bangladesh in December 1985. Kathmandu is wrong — it was later chosen for the Secretariat; New Delhi is wrong — the second summit was held there; Thimphu is wrong — Bhutan hosted a later summit.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the year of joining ASEAN by later members:

Brunei → 1984
Vietnam → 1995
Laos → 1997
Myanmar → 1997
Cambodia → 1999

How many years elapsed between the first expansion (after the 5 founders) and the last country joining ASEAN?
questions.explanation: The first expansion was Brunei joining in 1984, and the last country was Cambodia in 1999. The gap = 1999 − 1984 = 15 years. 12 years is wrong (miscalculation); 13 years is wrong (perhaps confusing with Vietnam to Cambodia gap); 17 years is wrong (uses wrong starting year).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are observer states of SAARC?

(i) China
(ii) Japan
(iii) European Union
(iv) United States of America

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: China, Japan, the European Union, and the United States are all observer states of SAARC. SAARC granted observer status to nine entities including these four along with South Korea, Australia, Iran, Myanmar, and Mauritius. Option '(i) and (ii) only' is wrong because it excludes EU and USA which are also observers; '(i), (ii) and (iii)' is wrong because it excludes the USA; '(i), (ii) and (iv)' is wrong because it excludes the EU.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement (AIFTA) came into effect in which year?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement (Trade in Goods) came into effect on 1 January 2010. 2008 is wrong — that year saw the signing of the agreement framework; 2012 is wrong — the services and investment agreement came later; 2014 is wrong — unrelated to AIFTA implementation.
